The plant{0D}
Location{0D}
The Tokugawa Moon Plant is\nlocated on the near side of the\nMoon in the Plato Crater,{0D}

which is itself situated on the
northern shore of Mare Imbrium,
the Moon's second largest mare.{80238057}Mare Imbrium means "Sea of
Rains".{0D}

The Plato Crater is approximately
100 kilometers in diameter, with
its smooth floor widely known as
 one of the darkest places on the
Moon.{0D}
It's a considerable distance to the\nnearest base, so you could say\nwe're pretty isolated here.{0D}
The only way to get here is by\nLSM from a Lunar-orbitin' space\nstation.{0D}
Energy{0D}
The plant is powered by solar\nenergy as well as helium-3\nnuclear fusion.{0D}
We gather solar energy through\nthe parabolic mirrors you were\nlookin' at.{0D}

Helium-3 is almost nonexistent on
Earth, but is found in relatively

 large quantities here on the
Moon.{0D}
We're able to obtain 1 ton of\nhelium-3 from every 100 million\ntons of Lunar regolith.{0D}

Helium-3 nuclear fusion, unlike
conventional nuclear fission, is a
virtually clean process that doesn't
 give off any secondary radiation.{0D}
Operations{0D}
There are numerous minerals\nfound in abundance on the Moon,\nsuch as ilmenite, for example.{0D}

We mine and process these, and
what we don't use here is
exported to Earth and space
 colonies such as Beyond.{0D}
Nearly all the materials used to\nconstruct the plant have come\nfrom Lunar resources.{0D}
After processin', the minerals are\nexported via the mass driver you\nasked about.{0D}

The Moon, with its low gravity,
ultra-low temperature and
high-vacuum, sterile
 environment, allows us to
manufacture Made on the Moon
drugs and other products with
 very high purity.{0D}

We've also been charged with
overseein' various life-science
experiments.{80238057}Since no organisms naturally exist
here, there's no risk of
contamination, and its vacuum
 environment also eliminates the
possibility of a biohazard occurrin'.{0D}

We carry out such
non-production-related
operations under the watchful eye
 of the United Nations Committee
on the Peaceful Uses of Outer
Space.{0D}
Staff{0D}
The employees we have workin'\nhere include computer engineers,\ngeologists, astronomers,{0D}
physicists, biologists, chemists,\nspace medical scientists, doctors,\narchitects,{0D}
and security officers such as\nmyself.  We're all employees of the\nTokugawa Group.{0D}

We have a li'l under sixty
employees total.{80238057}We're inspected by the UN twice a
year, but apart from that, it's just
us here.{80238057}There are no intervenin'
government organizations.{0D}

in the Moon Plant, numbered from
1 through 7.{80238057}Each factory manufactures a
variety of Moon-related products
'round the clock.{0D}

contain sensitive business
information, so I'm afraid I'm
 unable to show you inside any of
them.{0D}

helium-3 purification process in

The Moon{0D}
Data{0D}
The Moon's radius is 1,738\nkilometers, or one-fourth of\nEarth's.{0D}

Its average distance from Earth is
385,000 kilometers, and it proceeds
around its orbit at a speed of just
 over 1 kilometer per second.{80238057}Its gravity is one-sixth of Earth's,
and its mass one eighty-first.{0D}

A day on the Moon is equal to 27
days and 7 hours on Earth, takin'

 nearly 1 month to complete a full
rotation.{0D}

It's currently daytime here.{80238057}The temperature can rise as high
as 123 degrees Celsius in sunlight,
and fall as low as minus 233
 degrees in darkness.{0D}
Surroundings{0D}

To the far southeast you will find
Mare Tranquillitatis, or "Sea of
Tranquility," where Astronauts
 Armstrong and Aldrin landed near
the equator with Apollo 11.{0D}
The footprints they left behind\nhave been preserved, and are\nnow a famous tourist destination.{0D}
To the west of here, you can see\nthe beautiful Sinus Iridum, which\ntranslates to "Rainbow Bay".{0D}

Located just to the south is
Archimedes Crater.{80238057}A city that will house some 10,000
people is currently under
construction there.{80238057}It's scheduled to be completed in
about 10 years' time.{0D}
Development{0D}

It's been 70 years since the first
Apollo landin', and over 30 years
since man returned to the Moon
 and completed the first manned
Moon base, located in Oceanus

 Procellarum, or "Ocean of
Storms".{0D}

Goin' by the five-stage plan for
Lunar development proposed by

 German space engineer Dr. Krafft
Ehricke,{0D}

we have finally arrived at the
fourth stage, as we attempt to
expand manufacturin' capabilities
 and improve the livin' environment
on the Moon.{0D}
If a Lunar city can be successfully\ncompleted we'll be witnessin' the\nbirth of a new paradigm.{0D}

However, development on the far
side of the Moon is a different
story.{80238057}At present, it's only used for such
purposes as housin' radio
telescopes.{0D}
Origin{0D}
There are several theories in\nregard to the origin of the Moon.{0D}

The giant impact theory states that
the Moon is the result of a

 collision between celestial
bodies.{80238057}Then there's the fission theory,
which says that the Moon was
once a part of Earth.{0D}

There's also the coformation
theory, which states that the
Moon was formed out of the same
 gas as Earth.{80238057}Another theory, the capture
theory, says that the Moon was

 captured by Earth's gravitational
pull.{0D}
As of now, no theory has been\nproven correct.{0D}

If development on the Moon
advances to the point where we
can conclusively determine its
 internal composition, a definitive
answer should finally emerge.{0D}
